articles.headline: Lakers' Jeanie Buss accuses siblings of 'cloak and dagger' tactics
articles.description: Jeanie Buss accused her siblings of conspiring against her in court filings responding to her siblings' ongoing effort to sell their shares in the Lakers.
articles.headlineJa: レイカーズのジーニー・バス、兄弟らの「隠密な」策動を非難
articles.descriptionJa: ジーニー・バスは、レイカーズの株式売却を進める兄弟らに対し、自身に対して共謀していると法廷文書で非難した。
articles.body:
In a court filing this week, Jeanie Buss accused her siblings of conspiring against her in a "cloak and dagger" campaign through the media, said they were jealous that their father picked her over them to govern the Los Angeles Lakers and asked a judge to block her siblings' attempt to sell the family's shares in the team, which would end her run as the Lakers' governor.

Wednesday's filing, reviewed by ESPN, is the latest salvo in the bitter legal battle playing out between Jeanie and her siblings, namely Joey and Jesse Buss, leading up to a scheduled Dec. 8 hearing in Los Angeles Superior Court.

The filing responds to recent filings by Jeanie's siblings, who are seeking to sell the family's remaining shares of the Lakers to the Bob Iger and Josh Kushner ownership group, who are seeking to buy the team from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation.

"The conflicts that ensued after Dr. [Jerry] Buss's death [in 2013] were sadly inevitable, and no doubt intensified given that Dr. Buss chose his daughter over four sons to be his successor," Jeanie's lawyers wrote in the Wednesday filing.

"Respondents' obsession with tearing down Jeanie and their inability to accept that she would be a part of the Lakers' future is borne of this classic succession parable."

In 2025, Walter bought a majority stake in the Lakers from the Buss family at a $10 billion valuation. During that sale, the Buss family retained a 17.82% stake, just above the NBA's 15% minimum for the family to retain control. The family also received go-along rights. On Aug. 17, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Johnny, Jim, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss had voted to sell the remaining family shares to Iger and Kushner using those go-along rights.

Each sibling stands to make an additional $371 million if the family sells the entirety of its shares via the go-along provision.

Jeanie has attempted to block those attempts to sell, saying that her siblings must obey a 2017 court order that required the two co-trustees, Janie and Joey, to always vote to ensure she remained the controlling owner of the team.

In Wednesday's filing, she again asked the court to remove Joey and Janie as co-trustees of the trust for breach of fiduciary duty, to hold them in contempt of court, to find Jim, Johnny and Jesse liable for aiding and abetting a violation of the 2017 court order, and for her to be reimbursed for legal costs.

Sources close to the family have told ESPN that there have been settlement talks between the two sides, but it's unclear how much progress has been made leading up to the scheduled December hearing.

"Jeanie had no choice but to seek court intervention to enforce the clear terms of the trust and this court's 2017 order," Wednesday's filing states. "Respondents respond [by] casting themselves as victims, when in reality, the entire episode is their own false flag operation.

articles.headline: Patriots rule out A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson vs. Dolphins
articles.description: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. In addition, No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson has been ruled out due to an illness.
articles.headlineJa: パトリオッツ、ドルフィンズ戦でA.J.ブラウンとトレベイオン・ヘンダーソンを欠場
articles.descriptionJa: パトリオッツのワイドレシーバー、A.J.ブラウンが日曜日のドルフィンズ戦を欠場することが決まった。また、No.2ランニングバックのトレベイオン・ヘンダーソンも体調不良により欠場となる。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown has been ruled out for Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins, the team announced Saturday.

Brown had a knee issue flare up this week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

In addition, No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson has been ruled out due to an illness, according to the team. Henderson missed practice on Thursday and Friday.

The Patriots have one open spot on their 53-man roster and also could elevate up to two players from the practice squad by Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline. Fourth-year receiver Ryan Miller and first-year running back Lan Larison, both on the practice squad, are among the top candidates to be added to the game-day roster.

As for Brown, he was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and later that day, his designation on the injury report had changed. It noted the knee issue, in addition to the right high ankle sprain sustained in the season opener that had landed him on injured reserve.

"Just wasn't able to finish practice on Wednesday, so we continue to treat him," coach Mike Vrabel said Friday.

Prior to that practice, Brown acknowledged he was still managing the ankle injury and didn't have his trademark explosiveness on an every-play basis. But Brown made it clear he wasn't making excuses, adding, "None of that stuff matters. I'm out here, so I'm going."

The Patriots had Brown going as if he had never been sidelined due to the ankle injury sustained in the season opener. In his first action since being designated to return from IR on Oct. 14, Brown played 102 out of a possible 122 snaps in a win over the New York Jets on Oct. 18 and a loss to the Chicago Bears on Oct. 22.

He admitted the stretch of two games in five days was "a lot for anyone" and appreciated "the couple [extra] days [off] on the back end." He had expressed hope Wednesday he would have a full week of practice and "try to put my best foot forward on Sunday [in Miami]."

Then came the knee flare-up, which leaves the Patriots thin at receiver with DeMario "Pop" Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III the only healthy receivers on the 53-man roster.

Vrabel said the team's approach with Brown in the two games, and the injury that led him to miss Sunday's game, are "separate issues here."

Asked about the heavy workload for Brown, and if he would have benefited from fewer snaps, Vrabel said: "We want our best players to play and we consider him one of those."

Meanwhile, with Henderson out, the Patriots currently have just Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner as running backs on the 53-man roster.

articles.descriptionJa: まるでハロウィンのような驚きの展開が続いている。リサンドロ・マルティネスが退場した中でチェルシーがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドを2-0で下した一方、マンチェスター・シティはブライトンに対してつまずいた。
articles.body:
Happy Halloween! It's the final day of October, but there's still plenty of exciting matches to look forward to as we kick off a packed weekend of action across Europe.

In the Premier League's early game, Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 as Lisandro Martinez conceded a penalty and was sent off to pile more pressure on head coach Michael Carrick.

In the highlight of the midday fixtures, two in-form sides in Manchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion met just three days after their Carabao Cup encounter, but this time, it was the Seagulls coming out victorious with a 1-0 win. We then round off the day with a London derby as Tottenham Hotspur take on Crystal Palace, before Aston Villa take on Fulham.

Elsewhere across Europe, Atlético Madrid beat Levante in LaLiga, while the Bundesliga serves up a blockbuster Der Klassiker between league leaders Bayern Munich, led by newly crowned Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, and second-placed Borussia Dortmund.

Follow along for all the latest goals, updates and highlights from Saturday's matches.

articles.headline: Bournemouth run continues as James Trafford error costs Leeds
articles.description: A calamitous error from Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford set in-form AFC Bournemouth on course for a 2-0 Premier League victory at the Vitality Stadium.
articles.headlineJa: ジェームズ・トラフォードのミスが響きリーズが敗北、ボーンマスの快進撃が続く
articles.descriptionJa: リードのGKジェームズ・トラフォードによる痛恨のミスにより、好調なAFCボーンマスがバイタリティ・スタジアムでのプレミアリーグ戦を2-0で制した。
articles.body:
A calamitous error from Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford set in-form Bournemouth on course for a 2-0 Premier League victory at the Vitality Stadium.

The England international inexplicably gave away possession following a short goal-kick, allowing Justin Kluivert to set up Cherries forward Evanilson to score his fifth goal in six games in the 31st minute.

Substitute Amine Adli sealed Bournemouth's third successive top-flight success -- and sixth in all competitions -- in added time to lift them a point above Leeds in the table.

The visitors had been the better team before falling behind but could not prevent their winless run stretching to five top-flight games.

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was denied a goal on his 50th appearance for the club after his 11th-minute finish was ruled out for a handball spotted by VAR.

Visiting boss Daniel Farke, who celebrated his 50th birthday on Friday, watched his side create little on the south coast, with his disappointing afternoon compounded by a first-half booking.

articles.headline: Julio Enciso salvages a point for Ipswich Town at Hull City
articles.description: Hull maintained their unbeaten home record but saw their winless run continue after a cat-and-mouse 2-2 draw with Ipswich at the MKM Stadium.
articles.headlineJa: フリオ・エンシソがハル・シティ戦でイプスウィッチに勝ち点をもたらす
articles.descriptionJa: ハルはMKMスタジアムでのイプスウィッチとの激しい攻防の末2-2の引き分けに終わり、ホームでの無敗記録は維持したものの、勝ちなしの記録が続いた。
articles.body:
Hull maintained their unbeaten home record but saw their winless run continue after a cat-and-mouse 2-2 draw with Ipswich at the MKM Stadium.

Ipswich had the lion's share of possession in the first half, cutting through Hull's defence repeatedly and eventually leaving both Nobel Mendy and Konstantinos Tzolakis unable to prevent Florentino Luis' 22nd-minute opener as he sliced through on the right unhindered.

After 37 minutes the visitors looked to have doubled their lead as Julio Enciso headed the ball in from a corner, but the effort was disallowed for a foul on Oli McBurnie during the previous play.

Hull upped their game after the break and after 58 minutes Tim Iroegbunam raced down the right and fired home the equaliser.

The pattern of the game changed entirely and 10 minutes later McBurnie stepped up to a Hull free kick and slammed the ball beyond Christian Walton to give the Tigers the lead.

But it lasted only six minutes as Enciso worked his way through Hull's back line to produce a stylish leveller from just outside of the box.

articles.headline: Coventry out of relegation zone after stunning Sunderland win
articles.description: Coventry City climbed out of the relegation zone with a 3-1 win over Sunderland that leaves the Black Cats rooted to the bottom of the Premier League.
articles.headlineJa: コヴェントリー、サンダーランドへの劇的な勝利で降格圏を脱出
articles.descriptionJa: コヴェントリー・シティがサンダーランドに3-1で勝利して降格圏を脱出し、ブラック・キャッツ（サンダーランド）はプレミアリーグ最下位に沈んだ。
articles.body:
Coventry City climbed out of the relegation zone with a 3-1 win over Sunderland that leaves the Black Cats rooted to the bottom of the Premier League.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's first Premier League goal put Frank Lampard's side ahead 17 minutes in, Taiwo Awoniyi's first league goal for Coventry doubled the lead eight minutes before the break and Jack Rudoni all but killed it early in the second half.

Sunderland were offered a little hope when Enzo Le Fée sent Carl Rushworth the wrong way from the penalty spot in the 67th minute, but they grew increasingly frustrated and finished the match with 10 men as Omar Alderete was shown a second yellow card in stoppage time.

Lampard insisted this week it was too early in the season to worry about the table, but this was a much-needed win after last Saturday's disappointing 1-0 home defeat to Fulham, another side who had arrived at the CBS Arena in the bottom three.

Both of Coventry's first-half goals came after defensive mix-ups from Sunderland, who may be thriving in cup competitions with four wins from five, but who have only five points from nine Premier League games, and only one point from five on the road this season.

Regis Le Bris has welcomed the challenge of continental football this season, but his side have taken just one Premier League point since their Europa League campaign kicked off in mid-September, with this another afternoon where they will look back with regret at several missed chances.

Coventry had failed to score in five of their eight matches prior to this but took the first real opening that came their way with a little help from the visitors.

Trai Hume's half-hearted clearance of Milan van Ewijk's cross struck team-mate Luke O'Nien and fell for Sakamoto to arrow a shot into the far corner.

Sunderland should have been level six minutes later but Brian Brobbey dragged his shot wide with the goal gaping after too easily spinning away from Ethan Pinnock.

Coventry were looking much brighter than a week earlier. Viktor Torps' free-kick tested Robin Roefs, but the goalkeeper could do nothing when Awoniyi doubled the lead before half-time.

Again it was poor from Sunderland. After an ill-advised pass from Rigg, O'Nien too easily lost possession to Awoniyi, who charged his way past a couple of desperate challenges before beating Roefs with the help of a deflection off Alderete.

Coventry's confidence was high enough that Rudoni tried a bicycle kick shortly before a half-time whistle greeted with boos from the Sunderland end.

Things soon got worse for those travelling supporters as Rudoni's shot struck the unfortunate Alderete to put Coventry in control.

Chemsdine Talbi missed a fine chance moments after coming on, but Sunderland got a lifeline when Pinnock used an arm to block O'Nien's strike, Simon Hooper finally pointing to the spot after a lengthy spell watching replays before Le Fee hit an emphatic penalty.

articles.headline: Sources: Thunder no longer signing Ochai Agbaji following Chet Holmgren injury
articles.description: The Thunder are no longer signing free agent Ochai Agbaji as the franchise takes a step back to reevaluate its open roster spot after losing Chet Holmgren for two-plus months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: 【関係者】チェット・ホルムグレンの負傷により、サンダーはオチャイ・アグバジの獲得を断念
articles.descriptionJa: チェット・ホルムグレンが2ヶ月以上の離脱となるため、サンダーはロスターの空き枠を再評価することになり、フリーエージェントのオチャイ・アグバジの獲得を見送ると関係者がESPNのシャムス・チャラニアに語った。
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder are no longer signing free agent Ochai Agbaji as the franchise takes a step back to reevaluate its open roster spot after losing Chet Holmgren for two-plus months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Oklahoma City had agreed Friday to sign Agbaji to fill its open roster spot after major injuries to guard Cason Wallace and forward Jalen Williams, but then the Thunder decided to reconsider the options following the determination that Holmgren would also be out for an extended period.

Agbaji's health was not a concern or factor in the decision, sources said.

Agbaji, the No. 14 pick in the 2022 draft, has averaged 7.2 points and 2.7 rebounds in 263 games, including 108 starts. Agbaji, 26, was waived by the New York Knicks in final roster cuts this month. He has played for three NBA teams in his four years, splitting last season with the Toronto Raptors and Brooklyn Nets. Williams (fractured fibula, dislocated left ankle) and Wallace (torn labrum in left shoulder) both suffered injuries during Sunday's win over the LA Clippers that required surgery. Their recoveries will both take several months, but the Thunder have not ruled either player out for the season.

OKC expects Holmgren to return in eight to 10 weeks after undergoing biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear.

articles.headline: NFL scouts favor Drew Mestemaker as first QB taken in draft
articles.description: In a midseason poll of 25 NFL scouts, Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker was the overwhelming choice to be the first quarterback selected in the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
The on-field chaos of the 2026 college football season has rippled into the crop of top quarterbacks being evaluated for the 2027 NFL draft.

That QB class, once considered both flush with talent and deep, has taken a significant hit since the start of the season. Players such as Texas' Arch Manning, South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers and LSU's Sam Leavitt haven't shown themselves as surefire prospects.

ESPN conducted a midseason poll of 25 scouts and executives, asking who the top quarterback will be in next year's draft. Not surprisingly, the choppy play of top prospects yielded drastically different results from the August QB1 poll.

Seventeen of the 25 scouts in the midseason poll voted for Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker. The 17 votes are the most a quarterback has received in the three years ESPN has conducted the poll, with the overwhelming conviction about Mestemaker perhaps more a surprise than his general emergence. (Mestemaker got zero votes in the August poll.)

One scout summed up his vote this way: "Mestemaker seems like the only real choice at this point."

Notre Dame's CJ Carr came in second with four votes, followed by Miami's Darian Mensah with three and Oregon's Dante Moore with one.

It marked a significant shift from the August poll, when Moore had 14 votes, followed by Manning (seven), Sellers (two), Leavitt (one) and Carr (one).

The consensus among scouts is that this class isn't what it was billed to be after summer optimism. Much of that optimism stemmed from the cyclical nature of draft classes, as the last two featured underwhelming quarterback crops. There were two quarterbacks chosen in the first round in 2025 (Cam Ward at 1, Jaxson Dart at 25) and two in 2026 (Fernando Mendoza at 1, Ty Simpson at 13). That came after six quarterbacks went in the first round in 2024.

There still likely will be more than two quarterbacks picked in the first round in 2027 -- by virtue of need, if nothing else -- but any grandiose notions of this class have faded.

"Before the season, this class was going to rival 1983," a scout said of the fabled class where five quarterbacks went in the first round. "But there's been a lot of moving parts and Arch has fallen. It'll be interesting to see who resurfaces."

There's a distinct pivot point for this quarterback class: Mestemaker's 317-yard, two-touchdown performance against Oregon on Sept. 12. Oklahoma State won 39-31 as a nearly three-touchdown underdog, Mestemaker ran for a 75-yard touchdown that showcased his athleticism, and he completely outplayed Moore.

Mestemaker didn't start for his varsity high school team. His Disney movie rise from North Texas walk-on is fitting among QB prospect storylines in this draft that include Trinidad Chambliss' bootstrap story from Division II to Ole Miss and Mensah's moonshot climb from one FBS scholarship offer at Tulane.

Scouts love Mestemaker's whole package, as he has prototypical QB size at 6-foot-4, 211 pounds.

articles.headline: Saturday's fantasy basketball adds, NBA bets to make: Look to OKC's frontcourt
articles.description: Jim McCormick breaks down Saturday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Saturday

The NBA celebrates Halloween by featuring teams named after birds, bugs, bears, wolves, and even a type of music during today's seven-game slate.

A spooky element of Saturday's schedule is the heavy influence of injuries, even though it is still October. The Minnesota Timberwolves, for instance, are without offensive anchor Anthony Edwards for multiple months and are consequently massive underdogs against the San Antonio Spurs tonight. The Utah Jazz are without two important big men, while a hamstring injury to Ja Morant will change the Portland Trail Blazers' rotation in this matchup with Utah.

The Oklahoma City Thunder have been hit with waves of impactful injuries, the latest being All-Star pivot Chet Holmgren, who is sidelined for at least two months with a knee issue. Ajay Mitchell has already surfaced as a fantasy force in place of Jalen Williams, while a rookie center is relevant for today's game against the Houston Rockets.

This game in Houston (218.5) and tonight's meeting between the Philadelphia 76ers and Charlotte Hornets (215.5) both sport distinctly low point totals, serving as clear outliers among the other contests.

We can still identify helpful fantasy players and prop plays from these games, but the lower offensive ceilings should be noted when building DFS lineups. Through the lens of point totals, today's game in Charlotte is projected to have 12% fewer total points scored than tonight's meeting between the New Orleans Pelicans and Atlanta Hawks.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team

Players available in at least 50% of leagues

Isaiah Hartenstein, C, Oklahoma City Thunder (rostered in 23.5% of ESPN leagues)

It's not often we promote with several big men from the same team, but Holmgren's absence creates a major void for high-value two-way minutes. Hartenstein won't produce the block rate of his injured peer, but awesome rebounding and fun passing results are on the way now that he's the primary big in the rotation.

Jeremiah Fears, SG/PG, New Orleans Pelicans (41.6%)

articles.headline: Source: Commanders DT Daron Payne suffered season-ending foot injury
articles.description: Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in practice Friday, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in practice Friday, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The injury occurred late in a light practice, during a team drill, according to a team source. It was described as a fluke injury, not resulting from anyone stepping on his foot during a play.

Payne will be placed on injured reserve and calls his future in Washington into question. He's in the final year of his contract and turns 30 in May. A typical recovery for such an injury could take up to four months, according to medical experts. Payne is the Commanders' longest-tenured position player.

It's a tough blow for Washington (1-4-1) which plays the Eagles (2-5) Sunday night. The Commanders will already be without starting end Javon Kinlaw, out Sunday with a knee injury. They do have depth at the position with veterans Charles Omenihu and Deatrich Wise Jr. End Jer'Zhan Newton, a second-round pick in 2024, returned to practice this week after suffering a torn pectoral muscle during a preseason game on Aug. 14. He's listed as questionable for Sunday.

But Payne has been a longtime starter for Washington. In fact, he started every game between 2020 and '24 as well as the first six games this season. He missed only two games in 2025.

Payne made the Pro Bowl in 2022 when he recorded a career-best 11 sacks -- six more than his second best season. He had one sack this year but was averaging a career-best 2.8 pass rush wins per game according to Tru Media.

Washington drafted Payne in the first round of the 2018 draft and signed him to a four-year extension in March of 2023.
